paper.title: Automated confidence ranked classification of randomized controlled trial articles: an aid to evidence-based medicine
paper.citation: Cohen AM, Smalheiser NR, McDonagh MS, Yu C, Adams CE, Davis JM, Yu PS. Automated confidence ranked classification of randomized controlled trial articles: an aid to evidence-based medicine. J Am Med Inform Assoc 22(3):707-717 (2015)

inputs.name: PubMed 2026 baseline, pubmed26n0001-1334.xml.gz (SHA-256 of each file in output/baseline_manifest.json)
bow-20020213.tar.gz (McCallum's Bag-Of-Words library; its stopwords.c is the package's stop-word list)
Acute cholecystitis topic search, PubMed E-utilities, 2026-11-19 (output/cholecystitis_pmids.txt)

dataset.what: The paper's 'human-related' PubMed query is in its lost supplement. We use humans[mh] AND hasabstract AND english[la], 1987-2012, from the PubMed 2026 baseline
dataset.sensitivity: Chosen by RCT_PT count among four candidate queries (E-utilities, 2026-11-19): humans[mh] alone gives 312,580 RCT_PT citations, with hasabstract 301,496, with hasabstract and english[la] 284,086, against the paper's 277,789. Our dataset holds {dataset} citations, {dataset_rct} with RCT_PT, and {train_years} in 1987-2010 (the paper: 'over 5 million').

dataset.what: MEDLINE records as of the 2026 baseline, not the 2012-2014 download; old baselines are not distributed
dataset.sensitivity: NLM corrects publication types and MeSH over time. The RCT_PT count of our dataset is within {dataset_rct} of 277,789 (0.4%), so the drift in the label is small in total; which citations changed cannot be known.

dataset.what: Publication year: the PubDate year, or the first year of MedlineDate
dataset.sensitivity: PubMed's [dp] also matches electronic dates; the year split moves a few citations between training and test years.

dataset.what: The 7.5% training sample is drawn with NumPy seed 0; the paper gives no seed
dataset.sensitivity: {train_sample} citations, {train_sample_rct} with RCT_PT. A different sample moves the test measures by about the cross-validation spread (see the variants).

features.what: Feature sets: title and abstract uni-, bi- and trigrams, journal, author names, author count, author keywords (citation); MeSH descriptors, major descriptors, descriptor/qualifier pairs and substances (MeSH). The paper's list is in the supplement
features.sensitivity: The paper names the kinds (title n-grams 1-3, bibliographic fields, MeSH) but not the list. Our candidates hold 54 million features in the training sample against the paper's 'approximately 45 million'.

features.what: Tokens split on whitespace and punctuation, lower case, the SMART stop words of McCallum's Bag-Of-Words library, no stemming
features.sensitivity: From the same group's description of the same pipeline in 2018 (Cohen et al., PMC6146117), not from this paper.

features.what: Structured-abstract labels (BACKGROUND:, METHODS:) kept in the abstract text
features.sensitivity: Not tested; labels are a handful of tokens per abstract.

model.what: LIBLINEAR -s 1 (L2-regularized L2-loss SVM, dual), C = 1, with a bias term (-B 1), binary features without row scaling
model.sensitivity: LIBLINEAR's defaults; the paper states none of them. variants.json: C = 0.1, unit-length rows and logistic regression each move the 2011 measures; see the cause.

model.what: Forward selection with one 2-fold split per candidate instead of 5x2 CV; a set is added when it raises AUC at four decimals, F1 breaking ties
model.sensitivity: 5x2 CV at every step would take about 6 hours here; the final models are cross-validated 5x2 as in the paper. The paper does not say how AUC and F1 are combined; the rule follows the group's 2018 paper.

model.what: Confidence: Platt's sigmoid fitted to 2-fold out-of-fold margins of the training sample, in place of the paper's 'extension to the method of Ruping', which is described only in the supplement
model.sensitivity: Changes only the MSE rows. The zero-centred sigmoid baseline is the paper's own definition.

chisq.what: CHISQ filtering: Pearson's chi-squared test with Yates' correction, p < 0.05, over every feature of every candidate set; the paper gives no test details or threshold
chisq.sensitivity: The threshold sets the feature count of the CHISQ and POSTHOC columns ({n_chisq_c} and {n_chisq_m} against 102,023 and 113,177).

topic.what: The acute cholecystitis search: (cholecystitis[mh] OR cholecystitis[tiab]) AND acute[tiab], with the Robinson and Dickersin (2002) highly sensitive filter, 1987-2012, run on 2026-11-19. The paper's query (Table S2) is lost
topic.sensitivity: The topic terms are ours; the paper used the Cochrane review CD005440's terms. The search gives 1,409 PMIDs.

cause.summary: These estimates apply Fig. 1's manual-review rates (70%, 40%, 95%) to the disagreement counts. The rates come from 200 manually labelled articles that were never released, so they cannot be recomputed; putting the paper's rates into our counts would be a sensitivity variant, not a result. Their arithmetic is checked in text.arithmetic.

tables.summary: Rebuilt from the paper's text on the 2026 MEDLINE baseline: the feature-set list, the LIBLINEAR settings, the selection rule, the confidence method and the PubMed query are in the lost supplement, and NLM has corrected records since 2012-2014. Every AUC, average precision, F1 and accuracy is within 0.008 of the printed value (the largest gap: CITATION_ONLY F1 on 2012, 0.803 against 0.811), and our calibrated MSE within 0.001. The zero-centred sigmoid MSE is 0.007 to 0.009 higher than printed: it depends on the scale of the SVM margin, which the unstated C and feature scaling set.

table3.summary: As for Tables 1 and 2, and the CHISQ test is not described: at p < 0.05 our filter keeps {n_chisq_c} and {n_chisq_m} features against the paper's 102,023 and 113,177, so our CHISQ models are larger and score higher than the paper's, and our POSTHOC models, cut to the same count, are close to forward selection by construction. Our forward-selection models keep {n_feat_c} and {n_feat_m} features against 44,114,421 and 34,636,788, because selection kept more sets (abstract trigrams alone hold 35 million).

CITATION_ONLY kept: {chisq_c_kept}; refitted CHISQ {chisq_c_bonf_chisq}, POSTHOC {chisq_c_bonf_posthoc}. CITATION_PLUS_MESH kept: {chisq_m_kept}; CHISQ {chisq_m_bonf_chisq}, POSTHOC {chisq_m_bonf_posthoc}. The paper's counts and scores lie between our p < 0.05 and Bonferroni models, so its threshold lay between them; no threshold was fitted to the paper

page.lede: Cohen and colleagues released their RCT classifier only as a web service, which is gone. In November 2026 we rebuilt it from the paper and retrained both models on {dataset} MEDLINE citations of 1987 to 2012. Of {items} results, {exact} came back exactly, {agrees} agree, {partly} partly agree, {differs} differ and {not_attempted} could not be attempted. Every gap has a tested cause.
came_back: Retrained on the 2026 PubMed baseline, the MeSH model scores AUC {m_auc11} on 2011 (paper 0.973) and the citation-only model {c_auc11} (paper 0.966). Every AUC, average precision, F1 and accuracy of Tables 1 and 2 is within 0.01 of the paper's.
The human-related citations of 1987 to 2012 with an abstract in English: {dataset} citations, {dataset_rct} tagged as RCTs against the paper's 277,789.

Forward selection beats chi-squared filtering, dropping low weights costs almost nothing, and adding publication types raises AUC a little while average precision, F1 and MSE get worse, as in Table 3.
rctconf, a Python package with the feature sets, forward selection, the LIBLINEAR model and the confidence, with a tutorial.
buried: The supplement. Its feature lists, PubMed query, confidence method and Table S2 are not in PMC, and the publisher refused every request.
The manual review behind Fig. 1, the 2014 sample and the kappa. The 250 reviewed articles and their labels were never released.
The confidence method. Our fitted sigmoid comes within 0.001 of the paper's MSE, but the counts at 0.95 and 0.05 depend on the lost method and do not come back.
page.matched_intro: What the paper does not say, and what we chose.
matched: humans[mh] AND hasabstract AND english[la]: today it gives 284,086 tagged RCTs, nearest to the paper's 277,789 of four queries tried.
Title and abstract n-grams, journal, authors, author count, keywords; MeSH, major MeSH, MeSH with qualifiers, substances. Tokens as the same group described them in 2018.
LIBLINEAR with its default solver and C = 1. C = 0.1 gives the same numbers; unit-length rows raise AUC further.
One 2-fold split per candidate, AUC at four decimals. It keeps {n_sets_c} and {n_sets_m} sets where the paper kept 7 and 10.
A sigmoid fitted to out-of-fold margins, in place of the paper's extension of Ruping's method.
page.tables_caption: Each cell gives the paper's value over ours, from the committed full run. Shaded cells differ from the paper at its printed precision. CI rows are the Hanley and McNeil 95% intervals.
page.items_caption: Every table, figure and claim of the paper, with our numbers and the verdict check_results.py computes from them.
page.claims_line: The main claim holds: both rebuilt models rank RCTs with AUC near 0.97, the MeSH model ahead, as in the paper. The claims that do not match come from the lost supplement (feature sets, CHISQ test, confidence method) and from manual labels that were never released.
page.closing: The RCT Tagger came back from the paper's text and today's MEDLINE.
